[element-date]
=== `<date>` Date (in a citation)

Within a citation (such as <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>> or <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>), this element names the publication date of the cited source. All other dates within a citation should be tagged as <<element-date-in-citation,`<date-in-citation>`>>.

#### Usage/Remarks
The date model is an element-only model, and each date contains elements such as <<element-day,`<day>`>>, <<element-month,`<month>`>>, and <<element-year,`<year>`>>, which by Best Practice should always be numeric values.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-calendar,`@calendar`>>
* <<attribute-date-type,`@date-type`>>
* <<attribute-iso-8601-date,`@iso-8601-date`>>
* <<attribute-publication-format,`@publication-format`>>
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, <<element-related-article,`<related-article>`>>, <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>
#### Description

The following, in order: Optionally any one of: The following, in order: <<element-day,`<day>`>> <<element-day,Day (in a citation)>>, zero or one <<element-month,`<month>`>> <<element-month,Month (in a citation)>>, zero or one <<element-season,`<season>`>> <<element-season,Season (in a citation)>> <<element-year,`<year>`>> <<element-year,Year>> <<element-era,`<era>`>> <<element-era,Era (in a citation)>>, zero or one
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  date         %date-model;                                 >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(((day?, month?) | season)?, year, era?)
